runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix

runners_data.spotlight: 14-race maiden who has a very stiff task in this novice event.

races.paceDynamic: Skip To Victory will take the field along from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters in this 6-runner field. Vinciamo and Stoneacre Joe will sit prominent behind the leader, while Forest Phoenix, Gwen Tennyson and Aurora's Doublesix are all hold-up horses who need to come from behind. With only one front runner and three hold-up horses, this creates a moderate early pace that should quicken significantly in the final 2f. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners who can track Skip To Victory and kick clear when the pace lifts, as the hold-up horses face a tactical disadvantage with limited early pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Skip To Victory sets sustainable fractions without pressure from other pace-setters
scenarios.body: Vinciamo and Stoneacre Joe get perfect trips tracking the leader and have too much tactical speed for the hold-up brigade when the pace quickens. The three hold-up horses struggle to make up ground against runners with better positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Skip To Victory Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Skip To Victory's all-weather speed translates effectively to turf on debut
scenarios.body: The front runner gets away with soft fractions early and has enough left to resist the late challengers in a race that suits her confirmed pace-setting style. Her 5f specialization gives her an edge over rivals stepping back in trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Skip To Victory goes too fast early or fades dramatically on turf debut
scenarios.body: The pace becomes genuinely strong or the leader stops badly, creating gaps for the hold-up horses to exploit in the final furlong. Forest Phoenix and the other closers suddenly have something to aim at.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stoneacre Joe Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If Stoneacre Joe's Haydock flop was purely ground-related and he returns to Doncaster form
scenarios.body: The Tim Easterby runner settles better than expected and uses his proven 6f ability to outfinish rivals when stepped back to 5f. His recent good-ground form gives him an edge over the 5f specialists.

watchPoints.text: Skip To Victory could get easy lead and soft fractions with no other pace pressure, making her very hard to peg back
Forest Phoenix, Gwen Tennyson and Aurora's Doublesix all need hold-up rides but may lack sufficient early pace to target
Stoneacre Joe needs to bounce back quickly from disappointing Haydock effort just 9 days ago
Vinciamo returns from 51-day break with headgear change, fitness levels uncertain despite good recent work
Three Tim Easterby/Dylan Cunha trained runners suggest tactical pace battle between connections

runners_data.spotlight: Best run when second of four in a Musselburgh novice (5f, soft) on final start for Iain Jardine last October; yet to hit top form for new yard (6f/5f), but has been dropped 10lb.

runners_data.name: You Mystify Me

runners_data.name: Flybar

runners_data.name: Powernap

runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't run up to her best on her two runs this year, latest on the AW, having shaped with a degree of promise in a couple of nurseries last October; tongue-tie now tried; well drawn.

runners_data.name: Tanaka

runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on both runs for Kevin Ryan and no significant improvement after changing yards mid-season; back after a break but plenty to prove, particularly from outside draw.

races.paceDynamic: Flybar and I'm Dan Dare will ensure a strong gallop from the gates in this 5f sprint, with both confirmed early leaders likely to dispute the pace through the opening two furlongs. Six horses want prominent positions (Havin A Flyer, Moretons, With Glory, Sea Her Excel, You Mystify Me joining the leaders), creating significant congestion and tactical pressure approaching the final furlong. The hold-up horses O Fortuna, Powernap and Tanaka face a tough task from the rear given the likely honest pace and short trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure good early position without getting embroiled in the early speed battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders Flybar and I'm Dan Dare set sensible fractions without killing each other
scenarios.body: The prominent pack can settle nicely behind the pace-setters and strike approaching the final furlong when the leaders tire. Horses like You Mystify Me and Moretons are perfectly positioned to capitalize with their tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Flybar and I'm Dan Dare share the early work and one kicks clear at the right moment
scenarios.body: The winner comes from the front with tactical nous, taking advantage of fitness or class to hold off the prominent challengers. I'm Dan Dare's recent near-miss at Redcar suggests he's ready to strike.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the leaders/prominent pack tie up badly
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get a perfect setup with a collapse in front, allowing O Fortuna or Powernap to sweep through late. This requires the front group to go too fast early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If Flybar and I'm Dan Dare engage in a sustained speed duel from the start
scenarios.body: The entire field comes back to the closers as the early pace proves suicidal, creating opportunities for any horse with late kick. Even Tanaka could benefit from this chaos scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch for scrimmaging behind Flybar and I'm Dan Dare if six prominent runners bunch together approaching the two-furlong pole
Monitor I'm Dan Dare for signs of rustiness given recent yard change and whether cheekpieces again spark improvement
Observe You Mystify Me's early positioning on handicap debut as running style remains unclear from limited form
Check if Flybar shows any sharpness after 252-day absence given Hugo Palmer's stable form
Watch for Sea Her Excel's pulling tendencies compromising jockey tactics in the prominent positions

runners_data.spotlight: Modest form so far (ninth of 11 in a C&D novice last time) and looks more one for handicaps.

runners_data.spotlight: 13-2 when 17l fifth of six in a Newcastle fillies novice when with Karl Burke last November (6f); bought for 1,000gns three weeks later; plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer will take this field along from the front as the only confirmed pace-setter, setting what should be a sustainable tempo with no early pressure expected. Two Commanders represents the unknown quantity as a well-bred newcomer who could track the leader, while Grasmere Boy, Brouhaha, Pacific Glory and Gardening will all settle towards the rear given their hold-up styles. With five of six runners preferring to come from behind and only Mr Writer keen to race prominently, this creates a tactical advantage for horses that can sit handy and produce a sustained effort, rather than those needing a furlong to get organized from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Newcomer strikes gold
scenarios.trigger: If Two Commanders shows ability on debut and tracks Mr Writer before challenging
scenarios.body: The Edward Bethell newcomer gets the perfect tactical trip behind the pace-setter and his superior breeding tells. Hold-up horses find it difficult to make up ground with limited pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Standard setter prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer's class advantage proves decisive despite tactical pressure
scenarios.body: The Fanshawe runner controls from the front and has enough in hand to repel Two Commanders' challenge. His proven form at this level gives him the edge over exposed rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Grasmere Boy or Brouhaha produce late kicks to catch the front pair napping in a messy finish. The lack of early pace allows the hold-up horses to stay in touch longer than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace backfires completely
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer goes too fast early trying to secure his advantage
scenarios.body: The front-runner pays for aggressive tactics and weakens badly, allowing any of the hold-up horses to pick up the pieces. Pacific Glory or even Gardening could benefit from a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Two Commanders' market moves will reveal Edward Bethell's confidence in this well-bred newcomer's debut chances
Mr Writer's early fractions as he may overdo the front-running tactics if feeling pressure from Two Commanders
Grasmere Boy's position turning for home as hold-up horses need to be closer than usual with limited pace
Brouhaha's jumping from the stalls after being slowly away on debut at Southwell
Pacific Glory and Gardening struggling to get competitive positions if the pace becomes truly pedestrian

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer

runners_data.comment: 1-26; sound third over 1m4f on reappearance; below best three previous runs at around 2m

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue

runners_data.name: Captain Robert

runners_data.comment: Creditable run over 2m on AW this year; could go well but not at his best in 3 turf runs
runners_data.spotlight: Has been running creditably on the AW this year (in the frame on last three starts, all over 2m at Southwell); could go well, but below best three previous runs on turf.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner who prefers AW surfaces, 8 days since last run keeps her sharp but turf form is moderate
runners_data.comment: Over 6l behind Zephlyn over C&D last May; hasn't been in top form but place chance
runners_data.spotlight: Over 6l behind Zephlyn over C&D last May; some fair form since (won over 2m at Wolverhampton in October) but not quite at her best back on turf last twice (over 2m5f and 1m4f); place chance.

races.paceDynamic: Tracker Issue is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and will be allowed to bowl along at a comfortable tempo without pressure. The hold-up merchants Not So Sobers, Zephlyn, Fleur De Mer, Captain Robert and Lillistar will all settle behind, creating a bunched group tracking the leader. This will produce a slow early pace followed by a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs as the field closes on Tracker Issue. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours hold-up horses with a strong finish who can time their run perfectly in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Tracker Issue sets a pedestrian pace and the field remains bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses will have too much finishing kick for the tiring leader. Zephlyn and Captain Robert, both proven over the trip with good finishing speed, will surge clear in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Issue surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Tracker Issue maintains a steady gallop and the hold-up horses leave their run too late
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left in reserve to hold off late challengers who get caught flat-footed. His prominent running style suits the lack of early pace perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses make their move simultaneously in the straight creating traffic problems
scenarios.body: The finish becomes chaotic with horses getting blocked and hampered, allowing an outsider to slip through. Lillistar or Not So Sobers could benefit from a cleaner passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Tracker Issue goes too slow and gets swamped early by impatient connections
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl before exploding into a mad dash, suiting the horse with the best turn of foot. Captain Robert's AW form suggests he has the pace for this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Tracker Issue could steal this if he gets away with a slow pace and none of the hold-up horses can reel him in
Zephlyn's fitness after 58 days off - if fully wound up his course form makes him dangerous but the layoff is significant
Captain Robert's turf form as all his recent good runs have been on artificial surfaces at Southwell
The pace early on - if it's genuinely slow this becomes a lottery sprint finish where anything can happen
Traffic problems in the straight as five hold-up horses will all be making their moves in the same area simultaneously

runners_data.name: Holbache

runners_data.spotlight: Multiple sprint winner who runs here for the first time; 3lb higher than when last winning at Leicester (6f, good to soft) last September; not badly treated on that form but has yet to produce one of his better efforts following a break.

runners_data.name: Quercus

races.paceDynamic: Mark's Choice and Quercus are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead, with Ramon Di Loria and Holbache sitting prominent just behind. This creates an honest gallop over 6f at Catterick with sustained pressure from the start. The hold-up horses Good Earth, Wen Moon, and Evocative Spark will need to weave through traffic in the final 2f. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle, as the front runners will soften each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria or Holbache can track the early pace battle without getting drawn in
scenarios.body: The front runners will duel and tire, allowing the prominent horses to strike with perfectly timed runs. Ramon Di Loria is back on his last winning mark while Holbache has solid course form at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Artist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly breakneck between Mark's Choice and Quercus
scenarios.body: Good Earth or Evocative Spark can exploit the collapse of the pace battle with late runs. Evocative Spark arrives in red-hot form having won here twice already this season over 7f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Mark's Choice can establish a clear lead over Quercus early
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left to hold off late challenges in a race that doesn't develop the expected pace pressure. Mark's Choice drops 2lb and could find improvement on his first visit to Catterick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long Shot Special
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses or the favourites underperform
scenarios.body: Wen Moon or a returning Quercus could spring a surprise at bigger odds. Wen Moon has strong good ground form while Quercus loves this course despite recent poor form.

watchPoints.text: Mark's Choice and Quercus both want to lead which could create suicidal fractions over this sharp 6f trip
Good Earth may struggle to get competitive position from hold-up style if the pace is only moderate
Evocative Spark has won twice here this season but both over 7f so the drop to 6f is an unknown factor
Ramon Di Loria returns after 65-day absence which could blunt his finishing kick despite favorable weight
Holbache makes course debut after 144-day layoff with inexperienced 5lb claiming jockey taking over

races.paceDynamic: Agric Ranger will lead from the gates with no other confirmed pace angles in this field, creating a sustainable tempo that won't stretch the field early. The prominent runner will dictate terms without pressure, allowing the five hold-up horses to track him in a compact group through the early stages. This creates a straightforward tactical race where positioning into the straight becomes crucial, with the pace likely to quicken only in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can position close enough to strike, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for true hold-up horses to close from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Agric Ranger Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Agric Ranger gets an uncontested lead and maintains control of the pace
scenarios.body: The Tim Easterby gelding can dictate ideal fractions and prove hard to peg back when the field comes to him in the straight. His prominent style perfectly suits the race shape and his debut effort at Pontefract suggests more improvement to come.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses can get close enough to Agric Ranger turning for home
scenarios.body: Mademoiselle Belle or Battenburg Belle could benefit from the sustainable pace if they position within striking distance. The lack of early speed allows them to sit closer than usual and time their challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Agric Ranger's pace proves too slow and the race becomes a sprint from the three-furlong pole
scenarios.body: The field bunches up entering the straight and it becomes about who has the most natural speed in the closing stages. Zoustar Dreams could benefit from a truly-run sprint finish despite her poor recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies fail to fire and the race opens up for an improver
scenarios.body: Populus with cheekpieces or Mereside Spark returning from a break could outrun their odds if the pace sets up perfectly. The small field and moderate pace creates opportunities for lesser-fancied runners.

races.paceDynamic: La Tosca will take the field along from the start with no real pace pressure, as the only confirmed front-runner in this small field. Mohaasset and Favourite Friend may sit handy but both are more prominent racers than genuine pace-setters. The sustainable early gallop will create a tactical affair over the final 3f where positioning becomes crucial. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as they'll benefit from the modest pace and have plenty of cover to launch from.

scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows closers to get into perfect positions and the race becomes a sprint from 2f out where stamina and late pace matter most.
